chunks: "Whoever sends blessings upon Muḥammad and his family one hundred times between the two rakʿahs of al-Fajr and the two rakʿahs of al-Ghadāh, Allah will protect his face from the heat of the Fire. And whoever says one hundred times: 'Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent, and with His praise; I seek forgiveness from Allah, my Lord, and I repent to Him,' Allah will build for him a house in Paradise. And whoever recites twenty-one times
Allah will build for him a house in Paradise; and if he recites it forty times, Allah will forgive him."

key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer or its time
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ: an expression of glorifying Allah above all imperfection
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: the opening verse of Surat al-Ikhlas
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِهِ: Muḥammad and his family, upon whom blessings are invoked

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for salawat, dhikr, istighfar, and reciting Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad after Fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages acts of devotion in the period between the Fajr supererogatory prayer and the morning prayer, especially salawat, dhikr, seeking forgiveness, and recitation of Surat al-Ikhlas. It highlights the immense rewards of these practices, including protection from the Fire, a house in Paradise, and divine forgiveness.
